obligation: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard, as a service provider
citation: PCI DSS v4.0.1; ISO agreement; card brand rules
basis: The company transmits card data when staff key sales into merchants' virtual terminals and controls settings that can affect the security of merchants' card data (console users, log in as merchant, hosted payment page content). The ISO agreement requires the SAQ D for Service Providers and AOC each year and passing quarterly ASV scans. Visa service provider Level 2 (fewer than 300,000 Visa transactions a year). No size exemption
The sponsor bank registers the company with the card brands as an ISO under the ISO agreement

Treated as a financial institution: data processing and transmission of financial data for merchants (12 CFR 225.28(b)(14), incorporated by 314.1(b)). Customer information concerns fewer than 5,000 consumers (about 1,900 keyed sales a year; about 1,700 distinct cardholders in the call recordings, counted in P03), so 314.4(b)(1), (d)(2), (h) and (i) do not apply. Merchant owners are not consumers under 314.2(b)(1)

obligation: FTC notice of a notification event
basis: The 314.6 exception does not cover paragraph (j); notice to the FTC within 30 days of discovery for an event involving at least 500 consumers

obligation: Computer-Security Incident Notification Rule (bank service provider notice)
citation: 12 CFR Part 53; 12 CFR 225 Subpart N; 12 CFR 304 Subpart C
applies: No (company analysis; written confirmation requested from the sponsor bank)
basis: The company performs no service for the sponsor bank subject to the Bank Service Company Act; its services go to merchants and the processor partner, and the ISO agreement names no company service as a covered service. The ISO agreement's own 24-hour notice applies instead

obligation: Interagency Guidelines Establishing Information Security Standards
citation: 12 CFR 30 App. B; 12 CFR 208 App. D-2 and 225 App. F; 12 CFR 364 App. B
basis: The Guidelines bind the sponsor bank; they reach the company only through the ISO agreement's oversight terms
Not a credit union and serves none
No New York license, registration or charter. With fewer than 20 employees the company would also fall under the 500.19(a) limited exemption
Final rule not published; tracked for planning
Privately held LLC; not an SEC registrant
Terminals arrive already key-injected by the processor partner's key injection facility; the company holds no keys
The company holds personal information of Florida residents (merchant owners); about 92% of merchants are in Florida
Merchants are also in Georgia, Alabama and six other states; residency is checked for each affected individual at the time of an incident
Support calls are recorded; interception is lawful only with all parties' prior consent

obligation: FTC Act Section 5 (unfair or deceptive practices)
basis: The company makes claims to merchants about the fraud filter and sets automated decline thresholds that affect consumers' purchases
The fraud filter screens consumer purchases for online merchants whose customers may live in any state; applicability is to be assessed by counsel (P10)
